decision: LLD documentation format: 11 separate markdown files, each self-contained with ASCII flow diagrams, no external tooling required
reason: Engineer-readable, version-controllable, and easy to reference during development

decision: Interactive demo as single HTML file with vanilla JS, no frameworks or CDN dependencies
reason: Offline-capable, fast-loading, and simple for clients to open and understand without technical setup

decision: Demo excludes progress bars entirely from the frontend
reason: User explicitly stated 'no progress bars please in the whole frontend never use it'

decision: Demo uses hardcoded data and role-switching rather than backend integration
reason: Goal is client understanding and narrative flow, not functional API integration

decision: No progress bars in frontend UI
reason: User explicitly stated 'no progress bars please in the whole frontend never use it' — design should use alternative status indicators

decision: Interactive HTML demos instead of static slides or PDFs for client walkthrough
reason: Allows clients to experience the actual product flow and role-based perspectives interactively rather than passively viewing

decision: Separate artifacts for engineer understanding (LLD markdown files) and client understanding (interactive HTML + visual diagram)
reason: Different audiences need different formats; engineers need detailed specs, clients need narrative flow and visual architecture

decision: LLD documentation split into 11 separate markdown files by domain (auth, ingest, pipeline, database, API, workers, notifications, frontend) rather than single monolithic file
reason: Each domain is self-contained and independently understandable; engineers can reference specific files without context-switching

decision: Demo.html uses hardcoded data and vanilla JS (no frameworks, no CDN dependencies) to remain offline-accessible and lightweight
reason: Client-facing demo must work in any environment without setup; 1677 lines, 86KB is acceptable for single-file delivery

decision: No progress bars in frontend UI per user specification
reason: User explicitly stated 'no progress bars please in the whole frontend never use it'

decision: Project creation is manual, not automatic. Syndicate member explicitly creates project, uploads assets, then invites investors.
reason: User stated: 'when the syndicate gets a pitchdeck or some startup they are interested in... one person is going to create a project, add the assets of the project'

decision: Assets are any data file related to startup: pitch decks (PDF), audio (MP3), images (founder photos, locations), documents, spreadsheets.
reason: User specified: 'assets being any data file related to the startup, let that be pitchdeck, mp3 file or images of the founders or the places where they live'

decision: Information pool is shared with invited investors; they access all assets and can converse with system about them.
reason: User stated: 'there will be a set information pool that will be sent to each of the person that will be invited into the projects'

decision: Investor input is dual-mode: verbal (audio/transcription) or form-based; both are valid conversation channels.
reason: User specified: 'they can have a conversation with the system, let that be verbal or by form based they will put in their thoughts about the startup'

decision: Knowledge graph is constructed from all project assets (documents, images, metadata); system walks graph during retrieval to answer investor questions.
reason: User stated: 'when the information is being searched through during the conversation with each of the investor if we are showing a knowledge graph being walked from one node to other to search for the information that can be used to answer the question, the knowledge graph is the whole assets that being all the documents, images or excel information related to that thing'

decision: No progress bars in frontend UI.
reason: User explicitly stated: 'no progress bars please in the whole frontend never use it'

decision: [SUPERSEDED] Auto-project-creation on email receipt. Replaced by manual project creation workflow.
reason: User rejected original flow: 'the project will not get auto created after the call'

decision: Use Neo4j as the knowledge graph backend instead of Postgres pgvector adjacency tables
reason: Neo4j provides native graph traversal, better performance for complex relationship queries, and cleaner visualization of traversal paths for the frontend

decision: Remove email ingestion and auto-project-creation entirely
reason: Manual project creation gives syndicate members explicit control over what data enters the system; auto-creation was passive and error-prone

decision: Make asset upload the primary input mechanism, supporting any file type (PDF, MP3, images, Excel, video)
reason: Investors have diverse materials (pitch decks, founder recordings, location photos, financial models); a single asset type would be limiting

decision: Stream knowledge graph traversal to the frontend in real-time via SSE
reason: Investors need to see exactly which information the system used to answer their question; this builds trust and transparency

decision: Use D3.js force-directed graph for frontend visualization with node pulse and edge draw animations
reason: D3 is battle-tested for interactive graphs; force-directed layout makes relationships intuitive; animations make traversal visible without overwhelming the viewer

decision: Support both text and voice input for investor conversations via Whisper STT
reason: Investors may prefer speaking (faster, more natural); voice input removes friction and captures tone/emphasis that text misses

decision: Capture investor views through conversation itself rather than form responses alone
reason: Conversational input is richer (questions reveal thesis, follow-ups show depth of thinking); forms are rigid and often incomplete
